dossier.public_summary: The dip is very deep and implies a 21-Earth-radius object on a 3-day orbit around a small M dwarf, with odd and even eclipses of different depth. The depth changes wildly between sectors and even between transits, including near-zero dips, and the transit density is impossible for a planet.

reasons.why: Implied radius 20.94 Rearth is well above the planet regime; even undiluted depth 305400 ppm with rp/rstar 0.5526 implies a stellar-sized companion.

Depth is not steady even within one source (QLP). Sector 53 shows depth_ppm -27974 while others are 210607 to 316094 ppm, and transit_depths p_consistent 0.0 with chi2 13556.7 shows the variation is not sector-to-sector calibration.
Significant odd/even depth difference points to an eclipsing binary at twice the period, consistent with the density mismatch for a planet.

Transit density implied by dur 1.994 h and period 3.17 d is far from the TIC M-dwarf radius 0.347 Rsun; the star is a Gaia binary (ruwe 4.979, non_single_star 1) and the flat bottom shape alone does not overcome this.
reasons.value: fit_b 0.5825, star_density_penalty 119000, star_density_penalty_share 0.4025, fit_log_density_ratio -1.646, duration ratio 1.489

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip on the target (rules out a nearby blended EB), so the stellar companion is on the target, supporting EB over planet despite high xgboost planet_rank 0.05 and five similar planets.
